text:
The Fed didn't cut rates to zero in 2024. It cut the federal funds target range from 5.25-5.50% to 4.25-4.50% over three meetings: 50 bp in September, 25 bp in November, and 25 bp in December. The reason was that inflation had cooled toward 2% and the labor market was softening, so it began easing from a restrictive stance.

The two times the Fed took rates to near zero were December 2008 (financial crisis) and March 2020 (COVID). If you saw a claim about zero rates in 2024, it was wrong or referred to one of those episodes.
